=== aria-chart-role-img.yaml ===
title: 'feat(aria): add `role="img"` to chart container element'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Assistive technologies need a semantic hint that the chart container represents an image-like graphic region rather than an untyped generic element. Without that role, accessibility support is weaker even when aria labeling is enabled.


  ## Desired outcome

  Mark the chart container with `role="img"` so screen readers can interpret the rendered chart as a descriptive graphical object and pair it with the existing aria text more reliably.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A rendered chart container exposes `role="img"`, existing aria-label behavior continues to work on the same element, and visual rendering is unchanged.'

=== aria-label-data-exclusion.yaml ===
title: 'feat(aria): allows excluding data in aria-label'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Accessible chart descriptions can become noisy when datasets include raw coordinates, identifiers, or helper columns that are meaningful for computation but not for screen-reader output. Authors need a way to omit specific dimensions while keeping the underlying data intact.


  ## Desired outcome

  Let aria label generation exclude selected dataset columns through `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId`, so spoken descriptions can focus on the meaningful values without mutating the actual series data.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId` lists dimension indexes, those values are omitted from the generated aria label, the remaining values still appear in order, and reading back the series data shows it was not modified by aria generation.'

=== aria-ssr-safety.yaml ===
title: 'fix(aria): avoid throwing error in SSR mode'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Teams using ECharts for server-side rendering or prerendered output expect accessibility features to be safe to enable outside the browser. Right now aria processing can throw in SSR environments because DOM-only behavior is assumed even when no browser element exists.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make aria support safe in SSR mode so enabling accessibility metadata does not crash chart generation when ECharts is rendered without a live browser DOM.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Charts configured with aria can be created in server-rendered environments without throwing, browser rendering keeps its current accessibility behavior, and the fix does not require users to disable aria as a workaround.'

=== aria-test-20218.yaml ===
title: 'test(aria): fix test case of #20218'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The automated coverage for aria column exclusion needs to reflect the public option structure that users are supposed to configure. This is test-maintenance work, not a change to chart behavior.


  ## Desired outcome

  Update the regression test so it validates the supported public contract at `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId`, while keeping the existing user-facing aria behavior and data-integrity expectations unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The regression test exercises `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId`, still confirms excluded columns disappear from the generated aria label, still confirms source data is left untouched, and no runtime feature change is introduced by the test update itself.'

=== axis-custom-values.yaml ===
title: 'feat(axis): add `customValues` option to customize axis tick/label positions'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors sometimes need ticks and labels at hand-picked positions rather than at the axis scale’s automatically generated stops, for example when highlighting irregular milestones or business-specific checkpoints. Today this usually requires workarounds that can desynchronize labels from ticks.


  ## Desired outcome

  Allow both axis ticks and axis labels to opt into explicit positions through `customValues`, so authors can declare the exact values to show while still using the normal axis rendering pipeline.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Providing `customValues` on the tick or label configuration renders marks at the requested values, time axes handle those custom positions correctly, and charts that rely on automatic tick generation keep their current behavior.'

=== axis-ticks-grid-overflow.yaml ===
title: 'fix(axis): fix ticks overflowing grid area with dataZoom'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When dataZoom is applied, axis ticks near the visible edges can extend beyond the grid area and make a chart look visually broken even though the zoomed range itself is valid. Authors expect clipped or bounded ticks that stay inside the plotting region.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keep axis ticks contained within the grid when dataZoom changes the visible window, so zoomed charts look clean at the edges instead of drawing tick marks outside the plot area.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After zooming, edge ticks no longer overflow beyond the grid boundary, normal axis-tick rendering is preserved inside the plot, and unaffected non-zoomed charts keep their current appearance.'

=== bar-bordercolor-large-data.yaml ===
title: 'fix(bar): fix borderColor hides bar color with large data'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Large bar-series rendering can lose the bar fill when `borderColor` is configured, making bars appear incorrectly outlined or visually empty. This is especially noticeable in dense charts where the large-data path is chosen automatically.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix the large-data bar rendering path so `borderColor` does not hide the bar’s actual fill color.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Bars rendered through the large-data path keep their fill color even when `borderColor` is set, border styling still applies as expected, and standard bar rendering remains unchanged.'

=== bigint-data-handling.yaml ===
title: 'fix(data): avoid crashing with BigInt values'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Some chart authors pass data that includes JavaScript `BigInt` values from upstream business logic or preprocessing steps. Instead of gracefully interpreting or rejecting that input, ECharts can crash during value detection and parsing, taking down the whole chart render.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make data ingestion robust when `BigInt` values are present so charts no longer throw during value parsing, and users can either render supported numeric content or get normal downstream handling instead of a hard crash.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Supplying data that contains `BigInt` no longer causes an immediate exception in the parsing pipeline, and other supported numeric data paths continue to behave exactly as before.'

=== boxplot-encode-category-axis.yaml ===
title: 'fix(boxplot): correctly handle `series.encode` with category axis'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Boxplot charts can be driven from datasets and `series.encode`, but when a category axis is involved the encoded dimensions may be interpreted incorrectly. The result is a valid option that renders with misplaced or missing statistical boxes.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make boxplot series honor `series.encode` correctly on category axes so dataset-driven configurations map categories and box statistics to the intended dimensions.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A boxplot backed by dataset plus `series.encode` renders the expected categories and box values on a category axis, the encoded mapping no longer breaks the series, and existing boxplots without encode keep their current behavior.'

=== calendar-label-silent.yaml ===
title: 'feat(calendar): add `silent` option for `dayLabel`/`monthLabel`/`yearLabel`'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A chart author using the calendar coordinate system may want the day, month, or year labels to serve as static annotation rather than interactive elements. Today those labels still participate in pointer interaction, which can interfere with hover behavior on the actual calendar data and make embedded dashboards feel unexpectedly clickable.

  ## Desired outcome

  Calendar label interaction should be configurable independently for `dayLabel`, `monthLabel`, and `yearLabel`. When a user sets `silent: true` on any of those label configs, the corresponding rendered text should ignore pointer events while preserving the existing visual styling and positioning.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Authors can set `dayLabel.silent`, `monthLabel.silent`, and `yearLabel.silent` directly in the calendar option, and each one takes effect on its own. With `silent: true`, the label remains visible but no longer behaves like an interactive graphic element; with the option omitted or false, existing behavior stays unchanged.

  '

=== candlestick-non-normal-states.yaml ===
title: 'fix(candlestick): add back missing support for non-normal states since v5.0.0'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Candlestick charts support emphasis, blur, and select-style visual states, and users expect those non-normal states to continue working consistently across major versions. Since v5.0.0 some of that state handling was lost, so interactive styling no longer responds correctly.


  ## Desired outcome

  Restore the missing non-normal state support for candlestick series so hover, selection, and related state-based visuals behave again the way chart authors expect.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Candlestick items respond correctly in non-normal states, state-specific styling takes effect again without breaking normal rendering, and existing candlestick options keep their prior semantics.'

=== custom-renderitem-compoundpath.yaml ===
title: 'feat(custom): support compoundPath in custom series renderItem'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Custom-series authors sometimes need to return a composed path made from several subpaths as a single logical drawing element. Today `compoundPath` is not supported in `renderItem`, which blocks reusable vector shapes that are straightforward in lower-level graphics APIs.


  ## Desired outcome

  Support `compoundPath` as a valid custom-series element type so `renderItem` can return grouped path geometry in one element definition, provided `shape.paths` is supplied.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A custom series can return a `compoundPath` element from `renderItem`, `shape.paths` is honored when constructing the final graphic, and invalid compound definitions still fail clearly instead of silently misrendering.'

=== custom-series-installer.yaml ===
title: 'feat(custom): use installer for reusable custom series'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Reusable custom series should integrate like other chart types so wrapper libraries and modular builds can register them through the standard installation flow. This is an API ergonomics improvement for developers building on top of ECharts.


  ## Desired outcome

  Provide installer-based registration for reusable custom series so they can be added through the normal modular setup path rather than special-case wiring.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A reusable custom series can be registered through the standard installer flow, modular imports stay consistent with other chart features, and existing custom-series usage keeps working.'

=== dark-legend-page-text.yaml ===
title: 'fix(theme): fix legend page text color in dark mode'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  In dark mode, legend pagination text can retain an incorrect color that reduces contrast and readability against the theme background. Users experience this as a theme inconsistency in otherwise polished dark dashboards.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix dark-theme legend page text coloring so paged legends remain readable and visually consistent with the rest of the dark theme.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Legend page text in dark mode uses an appropriate readable color, pagination controls stay visible against the dark background, and light-theme behavior is unchanged.'

=== datazoom-handlelabel-show.yaml ===
title: 'feat(dataZoom): new option handleLabel.show'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Slider dataZoom handles can show useful value text while users interact, but some applications want those handle labels visible even outside active dragging or emphasis states. At the moment authors cannot explicitly control that visibility.


  ## Desired outcome

  Introduce `handleLabel.show` for slider dataZoom so teams can decide whether the handle labels are visible in the normal state, while `emphasis.handleLabel.show` continues to control the emphasized or dragging state separately.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Setting `handleLabel.show` toggles normal-state handle-label visibility, `emphasis.handleLabel.show` governs the emphasized state, and existing slider behavior is preserved when the new option is left unset.'

=== datazoom-movehandler-cursor.yaml ===
title: 'fix(dataZoom): change moveHandler cursor to default'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context
